title: Implantation of an Injectable Bone Substitute Material Enables Integration Following the Principles of Guided Bone Regeneration
authors: Barbeck M, Jung O, Smeets R, Gosau M, Schnettler R, Rider P, Houshmand A, Korzinskas T. 2020 Mar - Apr;34(2):557-568. doi: 10.21873/in vivo.11808.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss maxresorb / maxresorb inject (biphasic CaP) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “IBS can build a barrier -like structure 11 that is able to control the soft tissue influx into the central regions of the implantation bed, which could not be observed in other bone substitute granules of the same chemical composition. This directed integration behavior is assumed to be in accordan ce with the concept of Guided Bone Regeneration (GBR). Furthermore, BMGCs can significantly influence the process of angiogenesis within an implant bed of a biomaterial but not the maturity of blood vessels” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
